Technology stocks were firming Monday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding more than 0.8% in value while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was riding a nearly 0.8% advance.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Microsoft ( MSFT ) was trading higher Monday afternoon, rising almost 1% in recent trading, after the tech giant announced its $7.5 billion, all-stock purchase of GitHub, with both companies pledging to keep the focus at the developer platform on software creation as technology usage continues to grow. Microsoft will transfer corporate vice president Nat Friedman to the helm at GitHub while the target company's CEO and co-founder Chris Wanstrath joining the parent company as a "technical fellow" working on strategic software initiatives. Microsoft is expecting to close on the transaction by the end of 2018 and plans to use a portion of the $30 billion in available capacity for its stock buyback program for the acquisition. It also is expecting the deal will accretive to Microsoft's non-GAAP operating income by FY20.
In other sector news:
- Dell Technologies ( DVMT ) was back near its Monday break-even mark, recovering from a nearly 2% mid-morning retreat after reporting improved Q1 financial results compared with the same quarter last year. Net loss for the three months ended May 4 was $1.95 per share over a $2.29 per share net loss during the same quarter last year. Revenue grew to $21.36 billion from $18 billion during the year-ago period, topping the single-analyst call expecting $19.19 billion in quarterly revenue.
- Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) tumbled Monday, falling almost 4% in recent trading after the cyber-security company issued earnings guidance for its current Q4 trailing Wall Street expectations. Palo Alto said it is expecting non-GAAP net income for the three months ending in late July in a range of $1.15 to $1.17 per share, trailing the Capital IQ consensus by at least $0.04 per share. The below-consensus projection upstaged better-than-expected Q3 financial results, with Palo Alto earning $0.99 per share during the three months ended April 30, up from $0.61 per share during the same quarter last year and topping the analyst mean by $0.03 per share. Revenue rose to $567.1 million from $431.8 million in the year-ago period and also beat the $546.4 million analyst mean.
